The test image shows soybean leaves with tan/brown necrotic areas concentrated along leaf margins and tips, with some interveinal necrosis pattern. Green tissue remains near veins. This looks like it could be Sudden Death Syndrome, Bacterial Blight, or Brown Stem Rot.

Let me check reference images one at a time.
SDS reference shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis with yellow-green pattern. Somewhat similar. Let me check Bacterial Blight.
Not a match - bacterial blight shows small angular spots. Let me check Brown Stem Rot.
Brown Stem Rot shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis pattern - somewhat similar. Let me check Phytophthora.
Phytophthora shows complete plant wilt/death - not a match. Let me check Soybean Vein Necrosis Virus.
Not a match - vein necrosis shows small yellow/orange patches. Let me check another SDS reference.
Field overview - not useful. Let me check the third SDS reference.

Excellent match! SDS_268 shows the exact same pattern as the test image - brown/tan interveinal necrosis with green veins remaining and marginal necrosis. Let me view one more reference from Brown Stem Rot to compare.

Brown Stem Rot reference shows stem cross-section with internal browning - not matching leaf symptoms in test image.

**Summary of analysis:**
- Test image: soybean leaves with large tan/brown interveinal necrosis, green veins still visible, marginal/tip necrosis across multiple leaflets
- SDS reference (Soybean_Dise_268) is a near-perfect visual match - same brown interveinal necrosis with green vein network remaining
- SDS reference (Soybean_Dise_39) also matches well
- Brown Stem Rot shows similar foliar symptoms but the reference was stem-focused
- Bacterial Blight, Phytophthora, Vein Necrosis Virus all clearly don't match
